state_cpa_criteria: Experience with Illinois Department of Revenue audit representation|Knowledge of Illinois' flat tax rate and how it applies to crypto gains|Familiarity with Chicago city tax rules for crypto businesses|Experience with multi-state filings for remote workers
tax_notes: Illinois imposes a flat 4.95% income tax rate on cryptocurrency gains. For federal purposes, crypto is treated as property, and Illinois conforms to the federal treatment of capital gains. However, if you are a high-frequency trader, your crypto income may be classified as ordinary business income, which is also taxed at the 4.95% rate.
audit_triggers: The Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) actively cross-references federal return data. If you report crypto sales on your federal return but omit them on your Illinois return, the IDOR's automated systems will flag the discrepancy and issue an assessment.

state_cpa_criteria: Experience with FTB audit representation|Knowledge of California's community property rules for married crypto holders|Familiarity with California's non-conformity on like-kind exchanges|Experience with multi-state filings for remote workers
tax_notes: California has no preferential capital gains rate. Every crypto gain—whether held for five days or five years—is taxed as ordinary income at progressive rates from 1% to 13.3%. The top 13.3% bracket includes a 1% Mental Health Services Tax on income over $1 million. California also does not fully conform to federal like-kind exchange rules, and as a community property state, crypto acquired during marriage is divided 50/50 in a divorce.
audit_triggers: The FTB aggressively audits residency claims for high earners who leave California with unrealized crypto positions, scrutinizing the exact date of sale relative to the move. They also cross-reference 1099-B and 1099-DA data from exchanges to catch unreported crypto-to-crypto swaps.

state_cpa_criteria: Experience with NYS Department of Taxation and Finance|Knowledge of NYC city tax rules for crypto|Familiarity with BitLicense tax implications for business owners|Experience with multi-state filing for NY-based remote workers
tax_notes: New York taxes crypto gains as capital gains, with top state rates reaching 10.9%. If you live in New York City, you may also be subject to local city income tax, pushing the combined top rate even higher. New York also requires crypto businesses operating in the state to hold a BitLicense, which carries specific tax and reporting implications for business owners.
audit_triggers: New York aggressively pursues 'convenience of the employer' rules, meaning remote workers who claim residency outside NY but work for a NY-based crypto company may still owe NY state tax. The state also audits high-volume traders for failure to pay NYC estimated taxes.

state_cpa_criteria: Deep federal crypto tax expertise|Experience with Texas franchise tax for crypto businesses|Knowledge of multi-state filing for remote workers|Familiarity with IRS audit representation
tax_notes: Texas is one of the most tax-friendly states for crypto investors, as it does not impose a state income tax. This means you only need to worry about federal capital gains taxes. However, if you are running a crypto business, you must be aware of the Texas Franchise Tax, which applies to gross receipts above a certain threshold.
audit_triggers: While individuals face no state income tax, the Texas Comptroller aggressively audits crypto businesses and single-member LLCs to ensure they are not improperly using crypto holdings to avoid the Texas Franchise Tax (Margin Tax), which applies to gross receipts over $2.47 million.

state_cpa_criteria: Federal crypto tax expertise|Experience with Florida corporate income tax for crypto businesses|Knowledge of Florida sales tax rules for NFT and crypto sales|Familiarity with IRS audit defense
tax_notes: Florida does not have a state income tax, meaning crypto investors here only face federal tax obligations. However, Florida does impose a corporate income tax on businesses, and there are specific state sales tax rules that can apply to NFT sales and certain crypto services. Florida's lack of state tax makes it a popular residency for active crypto traders.
audit_triggers: The Florida Department of Revenue (DOR) aggressively pursues corporate income tax and sales tax collections. If you operate a crypto business (especially NFTs or metaverse real estate) and fail to collect Florida sales tax, the DOR can assess back taxes, penalties, and interest against the business owner personally.

state_cpa_criteria: Experience with Washington's capital gains excise tax|Knowledge of the WA threshold and how it applies to crypto|Experience with multi-state filings|Familiarity with federal crypto tax
tax_notes: Washington state has no standard income tax, but it recently implemented a 7% capital gains excise tax on long-term gains exceeding $270,000. This applies to cryptocurrency. Short-term crypto gains and ordinary income from staking or mining are not subject to this excise tax. Be sure your CPA understands how this threshold applies to your specific crypto portfolio.
audit_triggers: The Washington Department of Revenue is aggressively auditing taxpayers who move to no-income-tax states (like Texas or Florida) to avoid the 7% capital gains excise tax. If the DOR determines you were still domiciled in Washington on the date of the crypto sale, they will assess the 7% excise tax plus penalties.
